Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from examples instead of following fixed rules. The most common type is supervised learning. In this approach, we give the computer a large set of training data, which includes input examples and their correct answers. Using this data, the computer builds a model—a mathematical pattern that connects inputs to outputs.

Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. For instance, after training on photos of cats and dogs, it can guess which animal is in a new picture. Finally, we measure accuracy by comparing the model’s predictions with the correct answers. Higher accuracy means the model has learned the pattern well and can be trusted for real-world tasks.
